To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
BH4 peptids can be used to limit infarct size and improve cardiac function following AMI.

the BH4 peptide, which is a known anti-apoptotic peptide, can be conjugated to a CPP and a HP and that this peptidomimetic is able to cross biological membranes and to reach the myocardium in a mouse model of AMI.
BH4 peptic inhibitor of the mitochondrion-mediated apoptotic pathway is cardioprotective after a single bolous of intravenous injection in a murine AMI model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel therapeutic strategies to limit the extent of IR injury in AMI.
the development and evaluation of peptidic drugs for the treatment of IR injuries.
the design and the development of novel peptide-based therapeutic strategies for ischemia-reperfuson injury.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of CPP-conjugated antiapoptotic peptides is a promising strategy to protect cells from apoptosis and thus to treat ischemia reperfusion injury.
CPP-conjugated BH4 peptides are a new therapeutic tool for the treatment of ischemia-reprfusion injuries.
the use of peptidic inhibitors of apoptosis in the context of ischemia-reperfussion is a promising strategy for therapeutic applications in the field of cardiovascular diseases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BH4 peptides can be considered a new therapeutic approach in the management of IR injury in AMI.
BH4 peptide conjugated to a CPP is an efficient and safe cardioprotective agent that may have potential therapeutic applications.
BH4 peptides are able to protect cardiomyocytes from apoptosis in vitro, and that these peptides can be delivered to the heart after systemic administration in vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that
peptidic inhibitors can be used as therapeutic tools to protect cells against apoptosis.
the use of BH4 peptides conjugated with CPPs and HPs could be a promising therapeutic approach to limit IR injuries in AMI.
the use of peptidic inhibitors of the mitochondrial apoptogenic pathway, conjugated to CPPs and HPs, is a promising approach for the treatment of IR-injuries.
